posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Hey Joe, what ball park cost would it take to get this made as a model?

Hey, John. I would have to charge extra for the sheer distastefulness of it. It would cost a lot. As for my model-making methods, there's no real secret here. I usually just take a block of hard plaster, and start hacking into it with knives and files. Then I make corrections with more plaster, going back and forth in this manner, and stopping when the shape is correct.

posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** What formats can you use? What size will it print? I would have no problems coming up with data sets.

The holding plate allows about 10X10 inch base and maybe 8 inches high (about as tall as I've seen it). That is a heck of a lot of material though. If you would like a small object, I can slip that under the radar.

We use mainly STL here but I am sure other 3D formats are used. It really is a matter of what the pro-e (engineering software) will except, since that is where the file will be pulled up and where the size of the object is determined.

> **Colin Kaminski:** Also, do you think we could put a etalon in your spectrophotometer?

> **Colin Kaminski:** If I knew the FSR and Finesse I could calculate the rest of the design

I've only used a Fabry-Perot Spectrum Analyzer to determain FSR (which we don't have here). The spectrometer we use is to determine the wavelengths (and their relative intensities). I could be missing something, so I'll leave as, if you need any measurements I'll be happy to help.

Just in case, we do have a pretty good coffee machine as well
